title: PR 4786 - KV cache & batching refactor (scratchpad)
content:
Quick scratchpad for PR 4786 review - dumping notes, TODOs, and follow-ups.

TL;DR:
- PR changes: centralizes KV cache, introduces sharded cache + adaptive batching logic, changes eviction policy from LRU->cost-aware-LRU.
- Goal: reduce token compute by reusing prefixes across concurrency bursts.
- Risks: lock contention, memory amplification, subtle correctness around cache staleness across model variants.

Checklist (high-level):
- [ ] Correctness: unit + integration tests cover hot paths (cache hits/misses, model switch, sequence length edge cases).
- [ ] Thread-safety: verify lock granularity and absence of global locks on hot path.
- [ ] Performance: microbench for latency P50/P95 with and without batching; check tail latency.
- [ ] Memory: tooling to surface memory usage per-shard; test on 4/8/16GB configs.
- [ ] Rollout plan: canary config, fallback to old cache behavior.

Detailed notes / comments (copy into GH review):
1) cache/shard map (cache/shard_map.rs)
- line ~120: using Mutex<HashMap<..>> around the shard list. Potential contention: we should avoid taking this lock on every request path. Suggest swapping to RwLock or use lock-free double-checked insert pattern.
- TODO: measure contention under 500 rps synthetic load.

2) eviction policy changes (cache/evict.rs)
- cost-aware LRU idea is fine, but current cost calc uses token_count * model_weight. model_weight comes from ModelInfo::latency_score which is an estimate. Need unit tests that simulate different model_weights and confirm eviction order stable.
- risk: if model_weight is stale, we may evict frequently used small prefixes to make room for large-weighted ones -> regressions. Add metric: eviction_reason tag (size|cost|age) so we can observe in prod.

3) batching adapter (serving/batching_adapter.rs)
- critical path: batch formation must be O(1) per request amortized. Current implementation iterates all pending requests to find prefix matches (O(n^2) behavior). For large burst sizes this will blow up.
- suggestion: maintain index map from prefix-hash -> queue of candidate requests. That gives O(1) enqueue/dequeue per request and constant amortized work to form batch.
- TODO: spike to implement prefix map; bench against current in local-bench.

4) KV cache consistency across model variants
- PR stores cache entries keyed by (model_name, tokenizer_config, prefix_hash). Need to ensure tokenizer_config includes byte-level options (byte_fallback, special_tokens) — otherwise cross-model mismatches.
- Question: do we need to include sampling seed or generation params? I think not (cache is prefix-only), but note clearly in docs.

5) Metrics & observability
- Missing: per-shard hit/miss, avg_cache_entry_size, eviction_reason (see above), cache_hit_latency distribution.
- Add counters and tags in cache instrumentation. Avoid histograms on high-cardinality tags.

6) Tests
- Unit: add targeted tests for concurrent insert+evict stress tests (use loom or crossbeam test harness).
- Integration: add end-to-end test that runs model with prefix reuse and asserts token count goes down by expected factor in bench harness. Put in tests/integration/kv-cache-smoke.rs.
- Flaky test risk: tune timeouts; don't rely on sleeps in tests.

7) Performance numbers (author posted some in PR description)
- Author: "~18% token compute reduction on our internal chat workload". Need to reproduce locally: run bench script at tools/bench/kv_cache_bench.sh with 1/4/8 GPUs and real tracer enabled. Capture P50/P95 delta, not just avg.
- Note: in previous rollout, we saw P99 regressions due to batching reordering. Be explicit to check P99.

8) Backwards compatibility / migration
- Migration plan in PR: when upgrading, old cache entries remain unreachable because key format changes. Risk: sudden cache cold start -> increased token cost for initial traffic. Suggest optional compatibility mode to read old keys for 2 weeks.

9) Rollout & rollback plan
- Canary: 5% traffic in us-west, + 24h metric observation (hit rate, P95 latency, cost per token).
- Auto-rollback rule: if P95 latency increases >15% or cost per token increases >10% for two windows in a row.

Notes-to-self (quick):
- run `tools/bench/kv_cache_bench.sh --profile p95 --workers 16` before approving.
- add eviction_reason tag to metrics + ensure exporter supports it.
- ask Olivia to review instrumentation changes (she owns metrics infra).
- check memory accounting in allocator (we saw ~10% overshoot on 16GB VM last time).

Open questions for author (put into GH comment):
- Why switch to cost-aware eviction now vs keep LRU and tune size? historical context?
- Can we bound worst-case memory growth? current code permits short-term overshoot when many long prefixes arrive concurrently. Can we throttle insertions (circuit-breaker) or pre-evict?
- Is there any plan to persist cache across restarts? PR says no. If persistent later, key format needs stable migration story.

Follow-ups / owners:
- Add metrics: Olivia Park (owner)
- Add integration tests + runbench: Samir Shah (me)
- Implement prefix->queue map refactor in batching: author (cc: Avery)
- Add compatibility read for legacy keys (optional): infra/ops discussion needed

Acceptance criteria before merge:
- Thread-safety review + stress test green.
- No P99 regressions in canary (must be confirmed by bench).
- Metrics present with eviction_reason and per-shard hit rate.
- Clear rollback gating config in rollout yaml.

Random scratch TODOs (personal):
- capture flamegraph of batch formation (perf scope: batching_adapter::form_batch)
- add comment in code about tokenizer assumptions (so future authors know key composition)
- verify non-blocking path for streaming responses (should not hold shard lock while writing to client socket)

Other stray thoughts (brain dump):
- Maybe instead of cost-aware LRU, adopt hybrid: LRU with weighted aging factor that decays expensive-model entries gradually. Simpler to reason about and less dependent on accurate model_weight.
- Consider offloading large prefixes to remote cache (memcached/redis) for very large sequences to avoid RAM blowup; potential network cost tradeoff.

Local repro steps (notes to reproduce perf):
1) checkout PR: git fetch && git checkout pr/4786
2) ./tools/bench/kv_cache_bench.sh --workload chat-reuse --concurrency 512 --model small-a --warmup 60s --duration 180s
3) collect logs: /tmp/bench-*.log and upload to bench-s3 bucket for comparison

If I don't finish this review today: leave these flags on PR: request-changes (if tests missing) or comment (if tests present but need perf verification).

End scratchpad.

-- Samir
